meta.title: Guidebook: an everyday memory
meta.description: An example memory to learn retrieval with: a home, money, people, a side project, some code and its files, seen Today, Last year and Next year. Start with the "Start here" light.

perspectives.label: Today
perspectives.description: How things stand now: current money, the project as a prototype, Sam as a teammate.

perspectives.label: Last year
perspectives.description: A year ago: a shared flat, no car, the project only an idea, Sam a classmate. Some lines did not exist yet.

perspectives.label: Next year
perspectives.description: The plan: higher rent, more savings, Garden app launched, Sam a co-founder.

nodes.label: Start here
nodes.notes: This is the Guidebook: about 150 everyday things (a home, money, people, a side project called Garden app, a bit of code and the files that go with them). Nothing here is special — it is the kind of thing anyone keeps. Click a light to read it; the "Try" lights around this one each show one way of getting something back out. Press 1, 2, 3 to look at it as Today, Last year or Next year.

nodes.label: Try: ask by a word
nodes.notes: Press / and type a word you half-remember. Good ones here: tax, Sam, garden, insurance, pdf, passport, deadline, Lisbon, money, renew. The matches flare; things 1, 2 and 3 hops away glow dimmer and dimmer. The Results tab lists them by distance. Search reads names, values, tags, file names and paths, and these notes — so you rarely need the exact name.

nodes.label: Try: ask by neighbourhood
nodes.notes: Click a light and look at what is lit around it. Click Sam to see everything Sam touches: the project, a meeting, a birthday, a client. Click Files to see every file in this memory. Neighbourhood answers "what goes with this?" when you do not know what to search for.

nodes.label: Try: find how two things connect
nodes.notes: Press R and route from Idea to Launch. The declared timeline walks all 13 steps; today the memory finds a 3-step shortcut through Garden app and its client, the Riverside Co-op. Press 2 and try again: last year there was no client, so the best route is much longer. Then try Sam to Tax return (the money trail runs through an invoice), or Work laptop to Trip to Lisbon (the handbook decides the leave days). A route answers "how is this related to that?" Learn shortcut keeps the short way as a new line.

nodes.label: Try: look from another time
nodes.notes: Press 1 (Today), 2 (Last year), 3 (Next year). Rent, savings, the tax rate, the project status and who Sam is all change. Lights that disagree across time show small ghosts with the other values. Some lines only exist in some years: last year Sam had not met the Riverside Co-op yet, so the Idea → Launch route is longer.

nodes.label: Try: compute an answer
nodes.notes: Press P and run "Can I afford the trip?", then switch the lens and run it again. Today it says not yet, last year it was far off, next year it says book it — one rule, three truths. "Months until the trip" is a while loop; "What will checkout charge?" chains values from the code cluster.

nodes.label: Try: store your own
nodes.notes: Press N. Give it a name, a value, maybe a different value per lens, and link it to something already here. Useful first things to store: where you keep a document, a person and how you know them, a project and its next step, a file path, a number you keep looking up. Never store a password itself — store where it lives.

nodes.label: Questions this memory can answer
nodes.notes: Where is my lease? (search lease) · What costs me money every month? (search monthly, or click Money) · Who is involved in Garden app? (click Garden app) · What was the tax rate last year? (press 2, search tax) · What do I need before the trip? (click Trip to Lisbon; read its neighbours) · How does my job affect the trip? (route Work laptop → Trip to Lisbon) · What breaks if taxPct changes? (click taxPct, look at checkout) · What should I do about Bug #42? (click it; read its neighbours)

nodes.label: Five ways to get things back
nodes.notes: 1 By word: search. 2 By neighbourhood: click and look around. 3 By connection: route between two things. 4 By time or viewpoint: switch the lens and watch values change. 5 By computing: run a pathway that reads values and decides. Most real questions mix two of these.
